name: Start with CHIP-8
text: Start by drawing a digit. This complete program shows 5 and waits for a keypad key before returning.
source:
CLS
LD V0, 5
LD F, V0
LD V1, 10
LD V2, 8
DRW V1, V2, 5
LD V3, K
EXIT
expected: You should see 5 near the upper-left of the CHIP-8 display. Press and release X to return.
steps: Press Ctrl+P > CHIP-8 / assembly. Press F3 New and name it FIRST.
Type the program below, one instruction per line. Press F1 Save, then F5 Back.
With FIRST.asm selected, choose F4 Actions > Compatibility profile > SUPER-CHIP modern.
Press F2 Run. This profile supports the EXIT instruction at the end.
title: Run your first CHIP-8 program

name: CHIP-8 examples
title: How to use these examples
text: Begin with Run your first CHIP-8 program. Its picture and key wait make the result visible. Instruction reference pages show smaller fragments so you can see one operation at a time.
source:
LD V0, 7
ADD V0, 2
expected: In this fragment V0 becomes 9. It does not display a number and is not a complete ROM. Add fragments to a complete program before running them.

name: Save CHIP-8 source
title: Save and reopen your assembly
text: Keep the .asm file: it is the text you can edit. Running assembles a separate .ch8 ROM. Opening a .ch8 file does not turn it back into editable assembly.
source:
CLS
LD V0, 5
LD F, V0
LD V1, 10
LD V2, 8
DRW V1, V2, 5
LD V3, K
EXIT
expected: After reopening, the same source is there. Running it in SUPER-CHIP modern displays 5 and waits for a keypad key.
steps: Create an assembly file named SAVETEST and enter the program.
Press F1 Save, then F5 Back.
Select SAVETEST.asm and press F1 Open. F2 saves and builds/runs it.

name: Registers and numbers
text: Use V0 through VF to keep small numbers. Each holds 0 to 255; arithmetic wraps around when it goes past that range. VF also carries arithmetic and drawing flags. I holds a memory address.
source:
LD V0, 0x0A
ADD V0, 2
expected: V0 becomes 12.
title: Store and change a number
after: This instruction fragment changes registers; it does not print their values. Use Run your first CHIP-8 program for a complete visible example.

name: Labels and comments
text: Give a jump target a label ending in a colon. Keep its spelling the same wherever you use it. Add a semicolon comment to explain a line. Instructions ignore case; labels do not.
source:
JP start
start:
LD V0, 7 ; seven
expected: Jumps to start and sets V0 to 7.
title: Name a place in your program

name: Draw a digit
text: Point I at the built-in font with LD F,V0. The next DRW reads five rows of that glyph. Change the first number below to choose another hexadecimal digit, from 0 to 15.
source:
CLS
LD V0, 9
LD F, V0
LD V1, 10
LD V2, 8
DRW V1, V2, 5
LD V3, K
EXIT
expected: This complete SUPER-CHIP program displays 9. Press and release a keypad key to return.
steps: Create or open an .asm file and select SUPER-CHIP modern.
Type the example and press F2 Save & run.
title: Choose the digit to draw

name: Fonts and BCD
text: LD F,Vx chooses the small font glyph for a hexadecimal digit. For a decimal number with several digits, LD B,Vx writes its hundreds, tens and ones to three memory bytes. The fragment below splits 123 into 1, 2 and 3.
source:
LD V0, 123
LD I, 0x300
LD B, V0
expected: Memory 0x300..0x302 contains 1, 2, 3.
title: Work with fonts and digits

name: Keypad
text:
CHIP-8 expects sixteen hexadecimal keys. These PicoCalc keys provide them:

1 2 3 4   =   1 2 3 C
Q W E R   =   4 5 6 D
A S D F   =   7 8 9 E
Z X C V   =   A 0 B F

LD Vx,K waits for a press and release. Esc stops a running program.
source: LD V0, K
expected: Press and release X: V0 receives the CHIP-8 key value 0. This fragment does not draw the value.
title: Use the PicoCalc keypad

name: Delay and sound timers
text: Put a duration into ST to play a tone. The sound and delay timers count down at 60 ticks per second, so 30 ticks is about half a second. This complete program waits for the delay, then exits.
source:
LD V0, 30
LD DT, V0
LD ST, V0
wait:
LD V1, DT
SE V1, 0
JP wait
EXIT
expected: In SCHIP, plays for roughly half a second, waits for the delay and exits.
steps: Use SUPER-CHIP modern for this program.
Save the source and run it with F2.
title: Make a short sound

name: Assembly error
title: Fix an assembly error
text: Read the line number in the assembler message and check that line. For example, LD V0,256 is out of range: a byte must be 0 to 255. Correct it to the example below, then save and build again.
source:
LD V0, 7
EXIT
expected: In SUPER-CHIP modern the corrected program builds and returns. It changes V0 without drawing anything.
steps: Return to the editor and use F4 Tools > Go to line if needed.
Fix the instruction, then press F2 Save & run.

name: Blank CHIP-8 screen
title: A program shows a blank screen
text: Loading registers does not draw them. A visible picture needs I to point at sprite data and DRW to draw it. Check the selected profile as well. Try this complete program first.
source:
CLS
LD V0, 5
LD F, V0
LD V1, 10
LD V2, 8
DRW V1, V2, 5
LD V3, K
EXIT
expected: You should see 5. If it appears, compare your own font/sprite address and draw instruction with this example. Press and release X to return.

name: Profiles and compatibility
text: If a ROM draws or responds differently than expected, check its profile. From the assembly/ROM list, choose F4 Actions > Compatibility profile. Match the ROM first; changing its code should come later.
source:
LD V0, 8
LD V1, 2
SHR V0, V1
expected: VIP shifts V1 into V0, giving 1. SCHIP shifts V0, giving 4. VF receives the bit shifted out.
title: A ROM behaves differently
after: CHIP-8 (VIP), CHIP-48 (HP48), SUPER-CHIP modern and SUPER-CHIP HP48 differ in shifts, memory transfers and drawing. Use SUPER-CHIP modern for the complete programs in this guide. Their EXIT instruction is not part of classic CHIP-8.

name: CLS
text: Clear the display. Call it before drawing a new picture.
source: CLS
expected: The display is blank.
title: CLS

name: RET
text: Return to the instruction after the matching CALL. A RET without a call causes a return-stack error.
source:
CALL twice
JP done
twice:
ADD V0, V0
RET
done:
JP done
expected: Calls a subroutine, doubles V0 and returns. The final jump keeps it from falling into subroutine data.
title: RET

name: JP
text: Jump to an address or label. A jump back to the same loop repeats until Esc stops the program.
source:
loop:
LD V0, 5
JP loop
expected: Repeatedly sets V0 to 5. Esc stops the program.
title: JP

name: CALL
text: Run a subroutine at a label, then use RET to come back. Calls can nest up to sixteen levels.
source:
LD V0, 3
CALL twice
JP done
twice:
ADD V0, V0
RET
done:
JP done
expected: V0 becomes 6, then waits in the done loop.
title: CALL

name: JPOFF
text: Jump to the given address plus V0. Profile differences matter when you are adapting a ROM.
source:
LD V0, 2
JPOFF 0x204
LD V1, 1
LD V1, 9
expected: Jumps to 0x206, skipping the instruction that sets V1 to 1.
title: JPOFF

name: LD
text: Copy a value into a register, or move a value to or from a special register. V0 through VF hold bytes; I holds an address.
source:
LD V0, 12
LD V1, V0
expected: Both V0 and V1 contain 12.
title: LD

name: ADD
text: Add a byte or another register. ADD Vx,byte wraps without changing VF; ADD Vx,Vy sets VF when there is a carry. ADD I,Vx changes the address in I.
source:
LD V0, 250
LD V1, 10
ADD V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 4 and VF becomes 1.
title: ADD

name: SUB
text: Subtract Vy from Vx. A result below zero wraps around; VF is 1 when no borrow was needed.
source:
LD V0, 9
LD V1, 4
SUB V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 5 and VF becomes 1.
title: SUB

name: SUBN
text: Subtract Vx from Vy and leave the answer in Vx. VF is 1 when no borrow was needed.
source:
LD V0, 3
LD V1, 8
SUBN V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 5 and VF becomes 1.
title: SUBN

name: OR
text: Set a bit when it is set in either register. The answer replaces Vx.
source:
LD V0, 0x0A
LD V1, 0x05
OR V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 15.
title: OR

name: AND
text: Keep only the bits set in both registers. The answer replaces Vx.
source:
LD V0, 0x0F
LD V1, 0x03
AND V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 3.
title: AND

name: XOR
text: Toggle the bits in Vx that are set in Vy. The answer replaces Vx.
source:
LD V0, 0x0F
LD V1, 0x03
XOR V0, V1
expected: V0 becomes 12.
title: XOR

name: SHR
text: Shift right one bit and put the bit shifted out into VF. With one register operand, that register is both the source and destination. The two-register form depends on the profile.
source:
LD V0, 9
SHR V0
expected: V0 becomes 4 and VF becomes 1.
title: SHR

name: SHL
text: Shift left one bit and put the high bit into VF. The two-register form depends on the profile: VIP reads Vy; the other profiles read Vx.
source:
LD V0, 0x81
SHL V0
expected: V0 becomes 2 and VF becomes 1.
title: SHL

name: SE
text: Skip the next instruction when Vx equals the supplied byte or register. Otherwise continue normally.
source:
LD V0, 5
SE V0, 5
LD V1, 1
LD V2, 9
expected: Skips LD V1,1; V2 becomes 9.
title: SE

name: SNE
text: Skip the next instruction when Vx differs from the supplied byte or register. Otherwise continue normally.
source:
LD V0, 5
SNE V0, 6
LD V1, 1
LD V2, 9
expected: Skips LD V1,1; V2 becomes 9.
title: SNE

name: RND
text: Generate a random byte, then keep only the bits allowed by the mask. A mask of 0x0F gives a value from 0 to 15.
source: RND V0, 0x0F
expected: V0 is between 0 and 15.
title: RND

name: DRW
text: Draw sprite bytes from memory at I, using Vx and Vy as the position. Drawing uses XOR: set pixels toggle. VF reports a collision. Height 1 to 15 draws that many eight-pixel rows; Super-CHIP height 0 uses a 16x16 sprite. DRAW is another spelling.
source:
CLS
LD V0, 10
LD V1, 8
LD I, dot
DRW V0, V1, 1
JP done
dot:
DB 0x80, 0
done:
JP done
expected: Draws one pixel at logical (10,8). SCHIP low-resolution mode scales logical pixels on its 128x64 backing display.
title: DRW

name: SKP
text: Skip the next instruction if the hexadecimal key named by Vx is held. See Use the PicoCalc keypad for the physical keys.
source:
LD V0, 1
SKP V0
JP 0x202
expected: Waits here while key 1 is not held; pressing 1 skips the jump.
title: SKP

name: SKNP
text: Skip the next instruction if the hexadecimal key named by Vx is not held.
source:
LD V0, 1
SKNP V0
JP 0x202
expected: Skips the jump when key 1 is released.
title: SKNP

name: SAVE
text: Store V0 through Vx in memory starting at I. This is CHIP-8 memory, not an SD save. Reset I explicitly before a later load if you want code to work across profiles.
source:
LD I, 0x300
LD V0, 7
LD V1, 9
SAVE V1
expected: Memory 0x300 contains 7 and 0x301 contains 9.
title: SAVE

name: LOAD
text: Read V0 through Vx from memory starting at I. LD Vx,[I] is another spelling. Reset I between a SAVE and LOAD for portable code.
source:
LD I, 0x300
LD V0, 7
SAVE V0
LD I, 0x300
LD V0, 0
LOAD V0
expected: V0 returns to 7.
title: LOAD

name: DB
text: Put bytes into the program, usually for a sprite. Jump over the data so the machine does not try to execute it. Pad an odd byte count before the next instruction.
source:
JP start
image:
DB 0xF0, 0x90, 0xF0, 0
start:
LD I, image
expected: Defines three image rows and one padding byte; I points to them.
title: DB

name: DW
text: Put a 16-bit word into the program, high byte first. Prefer instruction names when writing code; words are useful when you need exact bytes.
expected: Emits bytes 0x60,0x07: the opcode for LD V0,7.
title: DW

name: EXIT
text: Stop the program and return to the calculator. Choose a Super-CHIP profile; classic CHIP-8 does not have this instruction.
source:
LD V0, 7
EXIT
expected: Returns after setting V0 to 7.
title: EXIT

name: HIGH
text: Choose the Super-CHIP 128x64 display and clear it. Use a Super-CHIP profile.
source:
HIGH
CLS
expected: Selects the higher-resolution display.
title: HIGH

name: LOW
text: Choose the classic 64x32 logical display and clear it. This mode-switch instruction needs a Super-CHIP profile.
source:
LOW
CLS
expected: Selects the classic logical display.
title: LOW

name: SCR
text: Scroll the display right. In high resolution it moves four pixels; low-resolution behaviour depends on the Super-CHIP profile.
source:
HIGH
SCR
expected: Moves existing high-resolution pixels right by four.
title: SCR

name: SCL
text: Scroll the display left. In high resolution it moves four pixels; low-resolution behaviour depends on the Super-CHIP profile.
source:
HIGH
SCL
expected: Moves existing high-resolution pixels left by four.
title: SCL

name: SCD
text: Scroll down by a number from 0 to 15. Use a Super-CHIP profile. Modern and HP48 profiles scale low-resolution scrolling differently.
source:
HIGH
SCD 2
expected: Moves high-resolution pixels down two rows.
title: SCD

name: FLAGSAVE
text: Keep V0 through Vx in the temporary Super-CHIP flag registers. Choose V0 through V7. These are not saved SD files.
source:
LD V0, 42
FLAGSAVE V0
LD V0, 0
FLAGLOAD V0
expected: V0 returns to 42.
title: FLAGSAVE

name: FLAGLOAD
text: Restore V0 through Vx from the temporary Super-CHIP flags. Choose V0 through V7.
source:
LD V0, 42
FLAGSAVE V0
LD V0, 0
FLAGLOAD V0
expected: V0 returns to 42.
title: FLAGLOAD
